brief: Personal site of an indie Mac developer. A visitor from X or GitHub sees in one screen what he makes (Dyno Chess, Adlib, app-growth-design, adlib-lyrics) and clicks through to one of them.

candidates.name: Desktop
candidates.concept: The page is a Mac screen and every project sits where it actually lives: Dyno Chess in the notch, Adlib in the top corner singing the intro, the skill and the mod in a Claude Code terminal.
candidates.typography: SF Pro (system) 13px menu bar / 24px lyrics semibold; SF Mono 12.5px terminal
traits: Hover the notch to open a chess island
The intro is sung word by word by Adlib
Risky on phones: it becomes an iPhone-style island + stacked windows

candidates.name: Tracklist
candidates.concept: An album back cover: one big sentence, then the work as a tracklist. Side A is Mac apps, side B is Claude Code. Hovering a track pulls it into focus and blurs the rest, Adlib's own effect.
candidates.typography: Helvetica Neue 500, 90px / -0.04em headline with the second line in grey; 30px track names; SF Mono 13px track numbers
traits: Full-width type then a ruled list
Black and white; colour only comes from product screenshots on hover
Headline focuses in word by word on first load
Scales to 20 projects without a redesign

candidates.name: Workbench
candidates.concept: Graph paper on a desk with each thing laid out working: solve a mate-in-one for Dyno Chess, watch Adlib sing, see the skill answer a question, the mascot dance.
candidates.typography: Charter 700 for names (26–34px), Charter 16.5px body, SF Mono 12–13px labels
traits: A playable mate-in-one on the home page
Warm paper with two night tiles
Most playful, least like a portfolio
